Live: First polling stations close in Kentucky, Indiana as exit polls set to beginUS Midterm Election 2026 Live Updates: Americans are polling on Tuesday in the crucial 2026 US midterm elections, a high-stakes contest that will determine which party controls the House of Representatives and the Senate for the remainder of President Donald Trump's second term. The elections are widely viewed as a referendum on Trump's presidency, his administration's policies and the direction of the country, with Republicans fighting to retain their grip on Congress after Iran war fallout, which has emerged as a major political and economic challenge for the administration. The conflict, its impact on global energy markets and Washington's handling of the war have added to the issues. Final pre-election opinion polls have given Democrats an upper hand, with several surveys putting them ahead of Republicans in the race. The outcome will determine how much legislative room Trump has during the final two years of his term. Currently, Republicans hold a 53-47 majority in the Senate, with 53 Republicans, 45 Democrats and two independents who caucus with Democrats. In the House of Representatives, Republicans hold 218 seats against 214 held by Democrats, while one independent member and two vacant seats account for the remainder. Democrats need to gain four net seats to take control of the Senate and three to secure a House majority. Stay with us for the latest updates from our reporter Rohit Sharma on the ground, along with developments reported by major US media outlets.
